dedupe_keys.name: bubbleran mx dt scalable digital twins of 5g and open ran networks

description: MX-DT is BubbleRAN's network digital twin product, announced on 25 February 2025 as an extension of its MX-ORS Open RAN platform. It creates one or more copies of a live 5G network, covering radio access, transport and core, in which operators can run what-if analyses, test optimisations and train AI models without disturbing the physical network. Built on Kubernetes, the twin is managed by a Digital Twin Operator in a separate operator plane: a Perceptor collects network state (topology held as Kubernetes custom resources, xApp databases and traffic) from the physical network, Replicators redeploy that state into synchronised or unsynchronised replicas, and a timing agent called Horaion manages synchronisation and lets users rebuild past states for fault diagnosis. Traffic is mirrored packet by packet through a RAN packet sniffer xApp and an MQTT broker. Results return to the real network only through standard O-RAN and 3GPP channels, for example as A1 policies to xApps. BubbleRAN validated it on its Multi-x 5G reference system. Coverage: networks built on BubbleRAN's platform or with open interfaces. Format and access: commercial product with public documentation. Caveats: tied to BubbleRAN's Kubernetes-based stack; traffic channel mirroring was planned for a later release. Simulation uses: risk-free testing of reconfigurations, failures and recovery actions on a twin of a mobile network. Related records: the Colosseum Open RAN digital twin and the VIAVI Network Digital Twin are comparable.
